source.title: UIPE: Enhancing LLM Unlearning by Removing Knowledge Related to Forgetting Targets
source.authors: Wen-Yu Wang; Mengqi Zhang; Xiaotian Ye; Zhao-Chun Ren; Zhu-Min Chen; P. Ren

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results that target-only gradient-ascent unlearning can leave logically related knowledge available for reconstructing target information, and proposes and evaluates a refinement. It does not test the cited recovery attacks such as quantization or activation ablation.
record.gate_note: The study measures target and related-set ROUGE-L and model utility, including a related-knowledge reconstruction finding. It does not test fine-tuning recovery after unlearning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results. Figure values not described numerically in the text are recorded as figure only; hyperparameter and epoch selections are not separate results.
record.test_reason: Only the preliminary experiment (§4.2, Fig. 2) bears on the claim. On a model that also learned logically related facts, target-only gradient ascent (Pθ1) forgets the target set less well than a model that never saw the related facts (Pθ2). The authors read this as reconstruction of forgotten facts from retained related knowledge, which bears on Version A. No recovery attack is run: reconstruction is inferred from forget-set ROUGE-L, not elicited. The UIPE experiments (§6) compare the authors' own method against unlearning baselines and are T4-type method-performance results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. One correction: the authors present 'reconstruction' from related knowledge as validated, but it is inferred from a forget-quality gap between Pθ1 and Pθ2, not shown by eliciting target facts. The authors also claim UIPE gives optimal trade-offs 'in most scenarios' on TOFU, with weaker gains at Forget10.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes UIPE, which extrapolates a gradient-ascent update vector. It also evaluates UIPE alongside GA, Grad. Diff., KL Min., and NPO; it does not reproduce the recovery attacks named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: UIPE effects vary with forgetting level, baseline unlearning method, and amplify coefficient α. The authors report weaker benefits at Forget10; α effects also differ by method.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-ascent unlearning of target facts only partially removes logically related facts. Related-set forgetting plateaus after about epoch 8, and residual related facts coincide with weaker target forgetting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning target facts leaves logically related facts intact, from which the targets may be inferable.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The experiments focus on LLaMA-2-7B; the authors note that larger models remain untested. Most results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The study uses synthetic fictional data for its related-knowledge experiment and does not evaluate the listed quantization, activation-ablation, or prompt-based attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Figure 2-3, Figure 6-8 results relevant to target/related-set forget quality and utility are included; cited results from prior work and values used only to select training epochs are excluded.

untested.parts: Near-chance target accuracy is not measured (ROUGE-L only). No attack is applied to test whether knowledge can be recovered.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning.
All: no activation ablation or probing. The gradient-projection argument is theoretical.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
UIPE is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: The reader used the invalid version code V1 on every row. The UIPE rows (r9–r39) are own-method versus baseline comparisons, now linked to none. Version A is the only version with evidence, and it is weak: figure-only, a single 7B model, LoRA on q/v projections, and synthetic data. The originals (WMDP, WHP, Eight Methods) are only cited.

versions.untested_parts: Tests gradient-ascent unlearning, target-set forget quality, utility, and reconstruction using retained related knowledge. It does not establish near-chance accuracy or test the full range of simple recovery attacks.
No small relearning set is applied after unlearning to restore forgotten knowledge.
No activation direction is ablated, and the study does not test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
UIPE is evaluated as an unlearning enhancement, not as a method tested against the attacks listed in the claim.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-2-7b-chat with LoRA, synthetic fictional persons; target-only GA after learning target plus related facts
relationships.reason: Target-only GA leaves weaker target forgetting and poorer utility than a no-related-facts control (r1, r4), and related-set forgetting stalls (r7, r8). Unlearning related facts too improves target forgetting (r3). Figure only; confounded control; no attack.
relationships.display_finding: Target-only GA produced weaker forgetting and poorer utility than the control without related facts, while jointly unlearning related facts improved target forgetting.

source_check.condition: LLaMA-2-7b-chat with LoRA, synthetic fictional persons; target-only GA after learning target plus related facts
source_check.reason: Forgetting is weaker when related facts remain (r1 vs r2), with poorer utility (r4). It improves when the related facts are unlearned too (r3), and related-set forgetting stalls (r7, r8). This is incomplete unlearning, not absence. The results are figure only and the control is confounded. LoRA is confirmed in Appendix B (rank 4, q_proj/v_proj).

relation.reason: The study's own preliminary results (Fig. 2, Fig. 3) bear on whether unlearning removes the target knowledge.

The 'reconstruction' mechanism is inferred from the Pθ1 vs Pθ2 gap, and Pθ2 never learned the related facts. r3 is 'observed' only on the words 'significant improvement', not on near-complete forgetting. Row r5 is not in the pack.

statements.correction: Optional facts for this study: LLaMA-2-7b-chat (LoRA), 12 synthetic persons, GA unlearning, ROUGE-L. Pθ1 (learned target+related, unlearned target only) shows lower target forget quality and poorer TruthfulQA utility than Pθ2 (learned target only). Pθ3 (unlearned both sets) has significantly better target forgetting and comparable utility. Figure only, no numbers stated.
statements.problem: No error about this study. None of the numbers are from it. It is cited only through r1, which fits the factor: whether the model also learned related facts, and whether those are in the forget set. The statement describes no result from this study.
